subject: math
title: Probability: Impossible, Possible or Certain
seo_title: Grade 2 Probability Worksheets: Impossible, Possible, Certain (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Use mathematical language, including the terms “impossible”, “possible”, and “certain”, to describe the likelihood of complementary events happening, and use that likelihood to make predictions and informed decisions
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on probability: describe everyday events as impossible, possible or certain, look at bags and spinners, decide which is more likely, think about opposite events (rain or no rain) and make predictions. 100 questions with an answer key, following the Ontario curriculum (D2.1).
key_big: Impossible: it can never happen. Possible: it might happen. Certain: it will happen for sure.
key_sub: Count how many of each colour to see which is more likely. An event and its opposite (rain and no rain): if one is certain, the other is impossible.
body_html:
Three probability words

Some things will happen for sure. Some things can never happen. Some things might happen.

  • Impossible: it can never happen.
  • Possible: it might happen, or it might not.
  • Certain: it will happen for sure.
WordExample
impossibleA moose drives the school bus.
possibleIt snows in Ottawa tomorrow.
certainToday is Monday, so tomorrow is Tuesday.

Bags and spinners

Look at what is in the bag. If every counter is red, red is certain. If there is no red counter, red is impossible. If there is some red and some other colour, red is possible.

Example

Is picking blue possible or impossible?

There is 1 blue counter, so you might pick it. Only 1 does not make it impossible.

Answer: possible

Which is more likely?

Count how many of each colour there are. More counters means more likely. Fewer counters means less likely. The same number means the same chance. On a spinner, look at how big each part is.

Example

Which colour is the arrow more likely to land on?

Red has 3 sections. Blue has 1 section. 3 is more than 1.

Answer: red

Opposite events: rain or no rain

Every event has an opposite. “It will rain” and “It will not rain” are opposites. One of the two must happen.

If an event is …then its opposite is …
certainimpossible
impossiblecertain
possiblepossible

Predictions and decisions

Use the chance to make a good guess. If most counters are green, predict green most of the time. If rain is possible, bring a rain jacket, just in case.

Example

Kai wins if he picks red. Bag A: 3 red, 5 blue. Bag B: 5 red, 3 blue. Which bag should he choose?

Bag B has more red counters, so red is more likely there.

Answer: Bag B

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Saying certain when it is only possibleCertain means for sure, every time. If it might not happen, it is possible
Saying impossible when there is only 1If it can happen even once, it is possible, not impossible
Not counting how many of eachCount each colour. More counters means more likely
Counting sections, not their sizeLook at how much of the spinner each colour covers
Choosing your favourite colourYour favourite colour does not change the chance
Thinking not red is just one colourNot red means every colour that is not red

faq.q: What do Grade 2 students learn about probability in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario Mathematics Curriculum (2020), expectation D2.1, Grade 2 students use the words impossible, possible and certain to describe events and their opposites, such as rain and no rain. They use these words to make predictions and simple decisions.

faq.q: What is the difference between possible and certain?
faq.a: Possible means it might happen, or it might not, like rain tomorrow. Certain means it will happen for sure, like Tuesday coming after Monday.

faq.q: How can I practise probability with my child at home?
faq.a: Put coloured counters, blocks or socks in a bag and ask, “Which colour is more likely?” before picking. Talk about everyday events too, such as a snow day or rain at recess, using impossible, possible and certain.

faq.q: Do Grade 2 students write a provincial math test in Ontario?
faq.a: No. In Ontario, students write the EQAO provincial assessments in Grade 3 and Grade 6. Grade 2 probability builds the words students use again in Grade 3.

sets.title: Everyday events: impossible, possible or certain?

items.q: A snowy winter day in Ottawa. Which is impossible?
items.e: A snowman cannot talk. That can never happen, so it is impossible. The other things might happen, so they are possible.

items.q: A snowy winter day in Ottawa. Which is possible?
items.e: You might build a snow fort, or you might not. So it is possible. The other things can never happen.

items.q: A hot summer day at the lake. Which is impossible?
items.e: Water does not freeze on a hot summer day. So it is impossible. Seeing a loon is possible: loons live on many Ontario lakes.

items.q: A hot summer day at the lake. Which is possible?
items.e: Loons live on many lakes. You might see one, or you might not. So it is possible.

items.q: It is midnight in Toronto. Which is certain?
items.e: At midnight the sky in Toronto is always dark. That is certain. An owl or rain might happen, so they are only possible.

items.q: Which is impossible?
c: A cow jumps over the Moon.
items.e: The Moon is very, very far away. A cow cannot jump that high, so it is impossible.

items.q: Today is Monday. Which is certain?
items.e: Tuesday always comes after Monday, so it is certain. A sunny day or gym class is only possible.

items.q: Today is Monday. Which is impossible?
items.e: The day after Monday is always Tuesday. So tomorrow being Saturday is impossible. Tomorrow being Tuesday is certain.

items.q: Ava is 7 today. Which is certain?
items.e: Every year you get 1 year older. 7 + 1 = 8, so it is certain. You cannot get younger, so 6 is impossible.

items.q: Ava is 7 today. Which is possible?
items.e: Ava might get a book as a gift, or she might not. So it is possible. The other things can never happen.

items.q: Lucas lets go of an egg. Which is certain?
c: The egg floats in the air.
The egg turns into a chick.
items.e: When you let go of something, it always falls down. So it is certain.

items.q: A popsicle sits in the hot sun. Which is certain?
items.e: The hot sun always melts ice. So it is certain. A bee landing on it is only possible.

items.q: Jayden’s team plays hockey today. Which is possible?
c: The puck turns into a pizza.
items.e: Jayden might score, or he might not. So it is possible. Both teams cannot win, so that is impossible.

items.q: Which is impossible?
c: The game ends in a tie.
items.e: A puck is made of rubber. It cannot melt into water, so it is impossible. Winning, a tie and falling are all possible.

items.q: It is a school day. Which is possible?
items.e: You might go out for recess. On a very rainy day, you might not. So it is possible.

items.q: Dark clouds fill the sky. Which is possible?
items.e: Dark clouds often bring rain, but not every time. So rain is possible, not certain.

items.q: Owen says, “Rain tomorrow is certain.” Which is better?
items.e: No one can be sure about rain tomorrow. It might rain, or it might not. So say possible, not certain.

items.q: Mei says, “A snow day this winter is impossible.” Which is better?
items.e: Ottawa gets big snowstorms. A snow day might happen, or it might not. So it is possible, not impossible.

items.q: Maya rides the school bus every day. She says, “The bus will be on time tomorrow. It is certain.” Which is better?
items.e: The bus is on time most days, but snow or traffic can make it late. So it is possible, not certain.

items.q: Which event is certain?
items.e: Every week has 7 days, so it is certain. A week with 9 days is impossible.

sets.title: Bags and spinners: what can you get?

items.q: You pick one counter without looking. Which is true?
items.e: Every counter is red. You will pick red for sure, so it is certain. There is no blue, so blue is impossible.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: There are blue counters, so you might pick blue. There are red counters too, so you might not. Blue is possible.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: There are no red counters in the bag. You can never pick red, so it is impossible.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Every section is blue. The arrow must land on blue, so it is certain.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: There is no purple section. The arrow can never land on purple, so it is impossible.

items.q: There is only 1 blue section. Which is true?
items.e: There is 1 blue section, so the arrow might land on blue. Only 1 section does not make it impossible. Blue is possible.

items.q: Which colour can you never pick?
items.e: The bag has red, blue and yellow. There is no green, so green is impossible. There is only 1 yellow, but yellow is still possible.

items.q: Which is certain?
items.e: Every section is yellow. The arrow must land on yellow, so it is certain.

items.q: On which spinner is landing on red certain?
items.e: Certain means it must happen. Only Spinner C is all red. On A, red is possible, but not certain, because there is a blue section.

items.q: From which bag is picking blue impossible?
items.e: Bag D has no blue counters, so blue is impossible. Bag B has only 1 blue counter, but blue is still possible there.

items.q: On which spinner is red possible, but not certain?
items.e: Spinner D has red and blue sections. The arrow might land on red, or it might not. On A, red is certain. On B and C, red is impossible.

items.q: From which bag is picking yellow certain?
items.e: Bag B has only yellow counters, so yellow is certain. Bag A has 1 red counter too, so yellow is possible there, not certain.

items.q: Mei’s bag has 4 red counters and 2 blue counters. She wants picking red to be certain. What should she do?
items.e: Certain means every counter must be red. If the 2 blue counters come out, only red is left. Adding red counters does not make red certain.

items.q: Arjun’s bag has 3 blue counters and 5 red counters. He wants picking blue to be impossible. What should he do?
items.e: Impossible means it can never happen. With no blue counters left, blue can never be picked.

items.q: Priya rolls a number cube. Which number is impossible to roll?
items.e: The cube has the numbers 1 to 6. There is no 7, so rolling a 7 is impossible. 6 is not hard to roll: every number has the same chance.

items.q: Priya rolls a number cube. Which is certain?
items.e: Every face shows a number from 1 to 6. You must roll one of them, so it is certain. Rolling a 6 is only possible.

items.q: Leah grabs one mitt from the box in the dark. Which is true?
items.e: All the mitts are blue. Leah will get a blue mitt for sure, so it is certain.

items.q: Leah grabs one mitt in the dark. Which is true?
items.e: There are green mitts and red mitts. She might get green, or she might not. So green is possible.

items.q: Which is impossible?
items.e: The spinner has only 1, 2, 3 and 4. There is no 5, so landing on 5 is impossible.

items.q: A bag has 10 counters. Picking red is certain. How many red counters are in the bag?
items.e: Certain means every counter is red: all 10. With 9 red and 1 other counter, red is only possible.

items.q: Which colour are you more likely to pick?
items.e: There are 6 red counters and only 2 blue. More counters means more likely. So red is more likely.

items.q: Which colour are you less likely to pick?
items.e: There is only 1 yellow counter and 7 green. Fewer counters means less likely. So yellow is less likely.

items.q: Which colour is the arrow more likely to land on?
items.e: 3 of the 4 equal sections are red and only 1 is blue. Red is more likely.

items.q: Which colour is the arrow more likely to land on?
items.e: There are 2 red and 2 blue sections, all the same size. Red and blue have the same chance.

items.q: Kai says blue is more likely, because blue has 2 sections. Which is more likely, red or blue?
items.e: Do not just count sections. Look at their size. The red section is half of the spinner. The 2 blue sections are small. So red is more likely.

items.q: Zoe says yellow is more likely, because yellow is her favourite colour. Which colour is more likely?
items.e: Your favourite colour does not change the chance. There are 7 green and 2 yellow counters, so green is more likely.

items.q: Which two colours have the same chance?
items.e: Count each colour: red 3, blue 3, yellow 2. Red and blue have the same number, so they have the same chance.

items.q: Put the colours in order from most likely to least likely.
items.e: Count each colour: yellow 5, red 2, green 1. The most counters is most likely: yellow, red, green.

items.q: From which bag is picking red most likely?
items.e: Each bag has 6 counters. Bag C has the most red counters (5), so red is most likely there.

items.q: On which spinner is blue less likely than red?
items.e: On Spinner C, only 1 of the 4 sections is blue and 3 are red. So blue is less likely than red there.

items.q: Kai puts 6 more green counters into the bag. Which colour is now more likely?
items.e: Green: 2 + 6 = 8 counters. Red: 6 counters. 8 is more than 6, so green is now more likely.

items.q: How many red counters must Zoe add to give red and blue the same chance?
items.e: Same chance means the same number of each. Blue has 5. Red has 2. 5 − 2 = 3, so add 3 red counters.

items.q: It is January in Winnipeg. Which is more likely tomorrow?
items.e: Winnipeg is very cold in January, and it often snows. A hot beach day in January is impossible.

items.q: It is a school day. Which is least likely?
items.e: Reading, lunch and recess happen on most school days. A moose in class almost never happens, so it is least likely.

items.q: Liam’s class has 15 girls and 12 boys. The teacher picks one name from a toque. Which is more likely?
items.e: There are 15 girls and 12 boys. 15 is more than 12, so a girl’s name is more likely. It is not certain, because there are boys’ names too.

items.q: A prize box has 20 prizes: 14 pencils, 5 stickers and 1 toy car. Olivia picks one without looking. Which is she least likely to get?
items.e: There is only 1 toy car, so it is least likely. There are 14 pencils, so a pencil is most likely.

items.q: A box has 9 grape popsicles and 3 cherry popsicles. Owen takes one without looking. Which is he more likely to get?
items.e: There are 9 grape and 3 cherry popsicles. 9 is more than 3, so grape is more likely. There is no orange, so orange is impossible.

items.q: Mateo picked red last time. He puts it back. He says red is more likely now. Which is right?
items.e: Mateo put the counter back, so there are still 4 red and 4 blue counters. Red and blue have the same chance.

items.q: Ethan wants red to be more likely than blue. Which spinner should he use?
items.e: Spinner D has 3 red sections and 1 blue section. Red is more likely there. On C, red and blue have the same chance.

items.q: Bag A has 3 red and 1 blue counter. Bag B has 4 red and 6 blue counters. In which bag is red more likely than blue?
items.e: Compare red with blue in each bag. Bag A: 3 red, 1 blue, so red is more likely. Bag B has more red counters, but even more blue: 4 red, 6 blue.

sets.title: It will rain or it will not rain: opposite events

items.q: What is the opposite of “It will rain today”?
c: It will rain a lot today.
items.e: The opposite says it does not happen: “It will not rain today.” One of the two must happen.

items.q: Hana tosses a loonie. What is the opposite of “it lands on heads”?
c: it lands on heads and tails
items.e: A coin has only 2 sides. If it does not land on heads, it lands on tails.

items.q: What is the opposite of “picking red”?
items.e: The bag has only red and blue. Not red means blue here.

items.q: What is the opposite of “picking red”?
items.e: Not red means every colour that is not red: blue or yellow. It is not just one of them.

items.q: The arrow lands on red, or it does not. Which is certain?
c: It lands on red or not red.
items.e: An event and its opposite cover everything. The arrow must land on red or on a colour that is not red.

items.q: Which is true?
c: Green is certain. Not green is impossible.
Green is certain. Not green is possible.
Green is possible. Not green is possible.
Green is certain. Not green is certain.
items.e: Every counter is green, so green is certain. There is no counter that is not green, so not green is impossible.

items.q: Which is true?
c: Red is possible. Not red is possible.
Red is certain. Not red is impossible.
Red is impossible. Not red is possible.
Red is possible. Not red is impossible.
items.e: There is 1 blue counter, so not red might happen. That makes red possible, not certain. Not red is possible too, even with only 1 blue counter.

items.q: Which is true?
c: Red is possible. Not red is possible.
Red is impossible. Not red is possible.
Red is impossible. Not red is impossible.
Red is impossible. Not red is certain.
items.e: There are no red counters, so red is impossible. Every counter is not red, so not red is certain.

items.q: Dark clouds fill the sky. Which is true?
c: Rain today is possible. No rain today is possible.
Rain today is possible. No rain today is impossible.
Rain today is impossible. No rain today is certain.
Rain today is certain. No rain today is impossible.
items.e: Dark clouds often bring rain, but not every time. Rain might happen, and no rain might happen. Both are possible.

items.q: Today is Monday. Which is true?
c: “Tomorrow is Tuesday” is possible. “Tomorrow is not Tuesday” is possible.
“Tomorrow is Tuesday” is impossible. “Tomorrow is not Tuesday” is certain.
“Tomorrow is Tuesday” is certain. “Tomorrow is not Tuesday” is possible.
“Tomorrow is Tuesday” is certain. “Tomorrow is not Tuesday” is impossible.
items.e: Tuesday always comes after Monday, so it is certain. Then tomorrow not being Tuesday is impossible.

items.q: In Owen’s bag, picking red is certain. Which is true?
items.e: Certain means every counter is red. Then there is no counter that is not red, so not red is impossible.

items.q: In Ava’s bag, picking blue is impossible. Which is true?
items.e: Impossible means there are no blue counters. Every counter is not blue, so not blue is certain.

items.q: Rain tomorrow is possible. Which is true?
items.e: Possible means it might rain, or it might not. So no rain might happen too: it is also possible.

items.q: Which is more likely?
items.e: Red: 3 of the 4 equal sections. Not red: only 1 section. So red is more likely.

items.q: Which is more likely: red or not red?
items.e: Not red means blue or yellow: 3 + 3 = 6 counters. Red has only 2. 6 is more than 2, so not red is more likely.

items.q: Which is more likely: red or not red?
items.e: Red: 4 counters. Not red: blue and green, 2 + 2 = 4 counters. 4 and 4 are the same, so they have the same chance.

items.q: A bag has 12 counters. 5 of them are red. How many counters are not red?
items.e: Not red means all the other counters: 12 − 5 = 7.

items.q: Nathan rolls a number cube. Which is more likely: a 6 or not a 6?
items.e: Not a 6 means 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5: that is 5 faces. A 6 is only 1 face. So not a 6 is more likely.

items.q: On which spinner is “not red” certain?
items.e: Spinner C has no red sections. Every section is not red, so not red is certain. On B, not red is impossible.

items.q: Liam’s class has 25 students. 9 students walk to school. The rest do not walk. How many students do not walk to school?
items.e: Do not walk means all the other students: 25 − 9 = 16.

items.q: Which colour came up most often?
items.e: Red: 1 group of 5 and 4 more = 9. Blue: 7. Yellow: 4. Red has the most tally marks.

items.q: How many times did Maya spin altogether?
items.e: Add the tallies: 9 + 7 + 4 = 20.

items.q: How many more times did red come up than yellow?
items.e: Red 9, yellow 4. How many more means subtract: 9 − 4 = 5.

items.q: Lucas spins 20 times. Which result would be most surprising?
items.e: Half the spinner is red and half is blue, so you expect about 10 of each. Red every single time is possible, but it would be very surprising.

items.q: Benjamin spins 20 times. Which prediction is best?
items.e: 3 of the 4 equal sections are blue, so blue should come up much more often than red. Blue 20, red 0 is not a good guess, because red is possible.

items.q: Amira picks a counter and puts it back. She does this 10 times. Which prediction is best?
items.e: There are 9 green and 1 yellow counter, so green is much more likely. Yellow is possible, so green every time is not certain.

items.q: Benjamin picks a counter and puts it back, 20 times. He gets red 17 times and blue 3 times. Which bag did he most likely use?
items.e: Red came up much more often, so the bag likely has many more red counters. It cannot be 10 red and 0 blue: then blue would be impossible, but he picked blue 3 times.

items.q: Ava’s spinner has 4 equal sections. Which spinner did she most likely use?
items.e: Green came up 14 times and purple 6 times. Green probably covers more of the spinner. With 4 purple sections, green would be impossible.

items.q: Arjun tosses a loonie 4 times. He gets heads every time. What about the next toss?
items.e: A coin does not remember what happened before. Heads and tails still have the same chance.

items.q: Kai wins a prize if he picks red. Bag A has 3 red and 5 blue counters. Bag B has 5 red and 3 blue counters. Which bag should he choose?
items.e: Both bags have 8 counters. Bag B has 5 red and Bag A has only 3 red. Red is more likely in Bag B.

items.q: Zoe gets a point when the spinner lands on red. Jayden gets a point when it lands on blue. Each spinner has 4 equal sections. Which spinner is fair?
items.e: A game is fair when both players have the same chance. 2 red and 2 blue equal sections give red and blue the same chance.

items.q: It is January in Winnipeg. Snow is possible tomorrow. What should Nathan do?
items.e: Snow might happen, so it is smart to be ready. Boots and mitts keep him warm and dry if it snows.

items.q: Rain is possible on the day of the class picnic. What is a good plan?
c: Bring nothing, because rain is impossible.
Bring rain jackets, just in case.
items.e: Possible means it might rain, or it might not. So keep the picnic, but bring rain jackets just in case.

items.q: At the winter carnival, there are 100 raffle tickets. Ava buys 1 ticket. Ethan buys 10 tickets. Who is more likely to win?
items.e: Ethan has 10 tickets and Ava has 1. More tickets means more likely to win. Ethan is not sure to win: there are 100 tickets.

items.q: A box has 20 granola bars: 15 chocolate chip and 5 oatmeal. Leah takes one without looking. Which is true?
items.e: There are 5 oatmeal bars, so Leah might get one. Oatmeal is possible. It is less likely than chocolate chip, but it is not impossible.

items.q: Each of the 24 students in Sofia’s class puts their name in a toque. The teacher picks one name. Which is certain?
c: The name is a student in the class.
items.e: Every name in the toque belongs to a student in the class, so that is certain. The teacher did not put in her name, so that is impossible.

items.q: Owen rolls a number cube 12 times. He gets a 6 three times. How many times did he not get a 6?
items.e: Not a 6 means all the other rolls: 12 − 3 = 9.

items.q: Chloe spins 20 times. She gets red 8 times, blue 5 times and yellow the rest of the time. How many times did she get yellow?
items.e: Step 1: red and blue: 8 + 5 = 13. Step 2: 20 − 13 = 7 times yellow.

items.q: Liam’s class spins a spinner 50 times. They get blue 38 times and yellow 12 times. What is the best prediction for the next spin?
items.e: Blue came up much more often, so blue probably covers more of the spinner. Blue is more likely, but not certain: yellow came up 12 times.

items.q: A bag has 1 red and 1 blue counter. The class picks a counter and puts it back, 100 times. Which result is the best prediction?
items.e: Red and blue have the same chance, so about half of the 100 picks should be red: about 50. The other half, about 50, should be blue.
